question: What must you do when you see this sign at a junction?
options: Stop completely in every case, because the sign works like a stop sign
Let vehicles on the intersecting road go first, slow down and stop if necessary
Give way only to traffic coming from the right, as with right-before-left
Drive on with priority, because the sign only warns of a junction ahead
explanation: Sign 205 obliges you to give way to traffic on the intersecting road, from both left and right. You must reduce speed early and stop if necessary. A full stop is required only if the traffic situation demands it. The obligation applies at the junction where the sign stands.
tip: Instructors want to see you slow down early and look both ways, not roll up to the junction at full speed. A hesitant, visible approach shows that you have noticed the sign. If you can see the road is clear, you may carry on without stopping.

question: Which statement is correct for this sign?
options: You may continue without stopping if no other vehicle is in sight
You must stop only if vehicles are approaching on the intersecting road
You must always come to a complete stop at the stop line, then give way
You must stop only when the sign is combined with a traffic light
explanation: Sign 206 requires a complete stop at the stop line (Haltlinie), even if the road is empty. If there is no line, stop at the point where you have a clear view of the intersecting road. Then give way to all traffic on that road and continue only when it is safe.
tip: A 'rolling stop' is a classic test failure. The wheels must stop moving, and examiners often watch for this. Stop at the line first, and if you cannot see well from there, creep forward and give way again.

name_en: Right of way at the next junction
question: What does this sign mean?
options: You have right of way on this road until a sign cancels it
You have right of way at the next junction only
You must give way to traffic from the right at the next junction
Right-before-left applies on this road from here on
explanation: Sign 301 tells you that you have right of way at the next junction or intersection. Its effect ends there. Beyond that junction, the right of way is no longer guaranteed by this sign.
tip: Do not assume the priority continues along the road. It does only with sign 306, which stays valid across junctions. Even with right of way, look at the side roads, because other drivers may overlook the signs.

question: Which statement is correct?
options: The sign applies only at the next junction
You must give way to traffic from the right at junctions
You have right of way at all following junctions until sign 307 or another sign cancels it
The sign allows you to drive faster than the usual speed limit
explanation: Sign 306 marks a priority road. You have right of way at following junctions and intersections until the priority ends, for example with sign 307. If the priority road turns, a Zusatzzeichen shows this and you must indicate accordingly. It does not change the speed limit.
tip: Where the priority road bends at a junction (a plate shows the thick line turning), you must indicate when you follow the bend, and also when you leave it by going straight on. Keep watching side roads: others may miss your priority.

question: What does this sign mean?
options: Your priority ends, and at the next junction the normal rules apply (usually right before left)
Your road ends and you must turn right
Priority is given to the road on the left from this point
The speed limit on this road is lifted
explanation: Sign 307 ends the priority road. After it, you no longer have right of way, and at the next junction the usual rules apply: right before left unless other signs or traffic lights regulate it. It does not itself give priority to another road.
tip: Your priority stops at this sign. Slow down before the next junction and look right: without other signs, rechts vor links applies there.

name_de: Kreuzung oder Einmündung mit Vorfahrt von rechts
name_en: Junction with priority from the right
question: What must you do when you see this sign?
options: Keep your speed, because vehicles from the right must give way
Stop completely, because the sign works like a stop sign
Prepare to give way to vehicles from the right at the next junction, and be ready to brake
Give way to vehicles from both the left and right, as the road is a minor road
explanation: Sign 102 warns of a junction where traffic from the right has right of way (right-before-left). Reduce speed and be ready to brake. It is a warning sign that makes you aware of the junction; the priority rule itself comes from §8 StVO.
tip: In 30 km/h zones in German cities, right before left is the normal rule and often has no sign at all. Examiners watch whether you slow down and look right at every unmarked junction.

question: Which statement about this sign is correct?
options: You must drive around the roundabout in the direction of the arrows (anticlockwise), and with sign 205 you give way to traffic in the circle
You always have priority over vehicles already in the roundabout
You must drive around clockwise, as in the UK
You must stop before entering, as with sign 206
explanation: Sign 215 is a mandatory sign: you must drive around the roundabout in the direction shown (anticlockwise). In Germany, vehicles in the roundabout have priority only if sign 205 is also present at the entry, which is normal. Without 205, ordinary priority rules apply.
tip: Check for sign 205 at the entry. Indicate when leaving the roundabout, not on entering when you want the first exit. Examiners dislike an unclear exit signal.

question: What must you do when you see this sign?
options: Drive through the narrow section first, because you have priority
Wait before the narrow section and let oncoming traffic pass first
Stop in every case, even if no vehicle is oncoming
Overtake slower vehicles before the narrow section
explanation: Sign 208 stands before a narrow section such as parked cars, roadworks or another obstacle. Oncoming traffic has priority there. If oncoming vehicles are in or approaching the narrow section, wait before it and proceed only when you can pass without obstructing them.
tip: Look ahead early and position your car so that you leave room for oncoming traffic. In city streets, an approaching bus or lorry can need more room than you expect.

question: What does this sign mean?
options: You must wait for oncoming traffic at the narrow section
Oncoming traffic has priority at the narrow section
Driving on the road is allowed only in one direction
You have priority over oncoming traffic at the narrow section
explanation: Sign 308 stands before a narrow section and gives you priority over oncoming traffic there. Oncoming drivers should wait for you. You still need to drive attentively and brake if they do not yield.
tip: Do not insist on your priority at the cost of an accident. When you have priority, watch for a driver who ignores it. Do not confuse this sign with 208, which has the opposite meaning.

question: What does this sign mean?
options: No parking in this street
The road is closed for all traffic in both directions
Only residents may enter this street
Vehicles may not enter from this direction
explanation: Sign 267 forbids vehicles to enter the road from your direction. You typically meet it at the far end of a one-way street, facing traffic that would drive in against the one-way direction. Exceptions apply only if a Zusatzzeichen allows them (often 'Radverkehr frei').
tip: Be careful with cyclists: a plate such as 'Radfahrer frei' (Zusatzzeichen 1022-10) can allow them to enter, but not motorists. Entering a one-way street the wrong way is a serious offence. Always check the signs at street corners in unfamiliar areas.

question: What does this sign mean?
options: No entry for vehicles coming from the right
One-way street: traffic may only travel in the direction of the arrow, here to the right
Compulsory turn to the right at the next junction
Priority for traffic coming from the right
explanation: Zeichen 220 marks a one-way street. Vehicles may only drive in the direction the arrow points, and the sign is placed at the junction where the one-way section begins. It applies until the street ends or the one-way section is lifted.
tip: Look for a Zusatzzeichen (e.g. 1022-10 'Radfahrer frei') under the sign, which allows cyclists to ride against the one-way direction. Without it, they are also prohibited. At the other end you will see Zeichen 267 (Verbot der Einfahrt).

question: What must you do when you see this sign?
options: Do not enter with a car, but motorcycles and bicycles may pass
Do not enter if you are driving a vehicle heavier than 3.5 t
Do not drive into this road with any vehicle, including bicycles
Do not enter from this direction, as it is a one-way street
explanation: Zeichen 250 prohibits all vehicles, including cars, motorcycles, mopeds and bicycles. Pedestrians may still use the road, and so may a person pushing a bicycle, who counts as a pedestrian. The ban applies from the sign, unless a Zusatzzeichen limits or exempts it.
tip: Read any Zusatzzeichen carefully, such as 'Anlieger frei' or 'Lieferverkehr frei', because the exceptions are what examiners ask about. Do not mistake this empty white disc for Zeichen 267, which is a white bar and only blocks entry from one direction.

name_de: Verbot für Krafträder, Mofas und sonstige mehrspurige Kraftfahrzeuge
name_en: No motor vehicles (motorcycles, mopeds and cars)
question: Which statement is correct?
options: Motor vehicles of all kinds, including motorcycles and mopeds, may not enter, but bicycles may
Only motorcycles and mopeds are prohibited; cars may enter
Only vehicles with more than two wheels are prohibited
All vehicles are prohibited, including bicycles
explanation: Zeichen 260 prohibits all motor vehicles: motorcycles, mopeds and Mofas, and cars and other multi-track motor vehicles. Bicycles and pedestrians may still use the road. The ban begins at the sign and applies unless a Zusatzzeichen allows an exception.
tip: A bicycle with a conventional pedelec motor (support up to 25 km/h) is legally a bicycle and may pass. A Mofa may not, which is a common trap for people coming from abroad. Do not mix this sign up with Zeichen 250, which bans all vehicles including bicycles.

name_de: Verbot für Kraftwagen und sonstige mehrspurige Kraftfahrzeuge
name_en: No cars and other multi-track motor vehicles
question: Which vehicle may pass this sign?
options: A passenger car with a trailer
A delivery van
A camper van (Wohnmobil)
A motorcycle
explanation: Zeichen 251 prohibits cars and other multi-track motor vehicles such as vans, lorries and camper vans. Single-track vehicles such as motorcycles, mopeds and bicycles may still pass. The ban applies from the sign, unless a Zusatzzeichen allows an exception.
tip: The picture shows a car, but the ban covers all multi-track motor vehicles, not just passenger cars. If the picture shows a motorcycle next to a car, it is Zeichen 260 instead, and motorcycles are banned there as well.

question: What must you do when you see this sign?
options: Reduce to 30 km/h, but only for the next 100 m
Not exceed 30 km/h from this sign until the limit is lifted or replaced
Drive exactly 30 km/h, as this is the minimum speed
Not exceed 30 km/h anywhere in the whole residential area
explanation: Zeichen 274 sets a maximum speed of 30 km/h, here a single-road limit. It applies from the sign until it is lifted by Zeichen 278 (Ende der Höchstgeschwindigkeit) or replaced by another speed sign, or until a Zusatzzeichen shows its end. Note that it is a limit, not a required speed.
tip: Be at the correct speed when you pass the sign, not shortly after. Instructors watch whether you brake early enough, and they expect you to check for time- or weather-related Zusatzzeichen. The round sign alone is not a zone, so right-before-left is not automatically in force.

question: Which statement is correct?
options: The limit of 30 km/h applies only on the road where the sign stands
It is a recommended speed that you may exceed in light traffic
From here, 30 km/h applies in the whole zone until the end-of-zone sign, and right-before-left usually applies
From here, 30 km/h applies, and you have priority over side roads
explanation: Zeichen 274.1 begins a Tempo 30-Zone. The 30 km/h limit applies on all roads in the zone, and the signs are not repeated at each junction. It lasts until Zeichen 274.2 (Ende einer Tempo 30-Zone) or another sign. Inside the zone, right-before-left generally applies, and there are usually no traffic lights or Zebra crossings.
tip: Do not look for a repeat sign after every junction: in a zone it will not appear, and the limit still holds. Examiners expect you to check right-before-left at every unsigned junction.

question: What does this sign mean?
options: The Tempo 30-Zone ends here; after this sign the speed limit that normally applies on that road is in force, such as 50 km/h in town
A new 30 km/h zone starts here
All speed limits end, and you may drive as fast as you like
The built-up area ends here, so you may drive 100 km/h
explanation: Zeichen 274.2 marks the end of a Tempo 30-Zone, and the sign appears on one side of the road only. After passing it the zone limit is lifted, and the speed limit for the road you are now on applies, normally 50 km/h inside a built-up area. Other signs may of course set a different limit.
tip: Leaving the zone often takes you onto a road with different priority rules, so check the junction signs and the right-before-left situation rather than accelerating immediately. A cancelled limit does not end the built-up area, so 50 km/h is usually still the maximum.

name_en: Start of a traffic-calmed area (shared space / living street)
question: What must you do when you see this sign?
options: Drive at most 30 km/h and keep to the right of the road
Give way to all vehicles from the right, but pedestrians must keep to the pavement
You may drive normally, but you may not park anywhere in the area
Drive at walking pace; pedestrians may use the whole road and children may play there, and you must not endanger or obstruct them
explanation: Zeichen 325.1 starts a verkehrsberuhigter Bereich. Vehicles must drive at walking pace (Schrittgeschwindigkeit), and pedestrians may use the whole width of the road, and children may play on it. Drivers must not endanger or obstruct pedestrians and must wait if necessary. Parking is allowed only in marked spaces, and the rules apply until Zeichen 325.2.
tip: The StVO gives no exact figure for Schrittgeschwindigkeit; courts usually accept around 7 km/h at most, so keep clearly slower near children. Examiners watch for hesitation and anticipation near pedestrians, and for illegal parking outside marked spaces.

question: What must you do when you see this sign?
options: You may now drive at 50 km/h and have priority
You are leaving the traffic-calmed area and must give way to traffic on the road you are entering
Pedestrians must give way to you from here on, and priority comes from the right
You may now park anywhere along the road
explanation: Zeichen 325.2 ends the traffic-calmed area, so the special rules (walking pace, pedestrian use of the whole road) no longer apply. When you drive out of this area onto another road, you must give way to other road users (§ 10 StVO). From here the normal rules and signs for the road apply.
tip: A common mistake is to accelerate at once and pull out without giving way, because people assume they have right of way after the sign. Examiners expect you to stop or slow down, look both ways and also watch for cyclists and pedestrians on the pavement before you move out.

name_en: Town/village name sign (front: start of built-up area)
question: What does this sign mean?
options: A recommended route to the named town
The end of the built-up area and the town named
You are entering a built-up area; the in-town rules apply, including a general 50 km/h limit unless signs show otherwise
A tourist information sign without legal effect
explanation: Zeichen 310 (the yellow Ortstafel, front side) marks the beginning of a closed built-up area (geschlossene Ortschaft). From the sign the in-town rules apply, including the general limit of 50 km/h for motor vehicles unless other signs set a different limit. The area ends at the back of the sign, Zeichen 311.
tip: Brake before the sign, not at it, because speed checks are often placed just behind Ortstafeln. Also keep in mind that if a lower limit was signed before the town, that remains in force. The yellow sign has legal effect and is not just a name board, which is why it is a favourite exam question.

name_en: Town sign, reverse side: end of built-up area
question: What does this sign mean?
options: You are entering a built-up area, so the 50 km/h limit now applies.
You are leaving the built-up area (geschlossene Ortschaft), so the town rules no longer apply from here.
A town district ends, but the town-specific rules continue.
A speed limit applies until the next village sign.
explanation: The back of the town sign (Zeichen 311) marks the end of the geschlossene Ortschaft. From here the rules for roads outside built-up areas apply. For cars without a trailer the general limit is then 100 km/h on ordinary roads. The sign does not cancel speed limits that are signposted separately.
tip: Do not speed up before you pass the sign. Speed checks are often set up just behind it, and instructors want to see your speed adapted to the road, not just to the sign. A separate speed-limit sign stays valid after the town sign.

name_en: No overtaking for motor vehicles of all kinds
question: What must you do when you see this sign?
options: You may only overtake vehicles that are slower than 25 km/h.
You must not overtake any vehicle at all, including bicycles and motorcycles.
Motor vehicles must not overtake multi-track motor vehicles (cars, vans, lorries), but may still overtake bicycles and solo motorcycles.
Only lorries over 3.5 t are forbidden to overtake.
explanation: Zeichen 276 forbids motor vehicles of all kinds from overtaking multi-track vehicles and motorcycles with a sidecar. Single-track vehicles such as bicycles and solo motorcycles may still be overtaken. The ban lasts until a sign ending it, such as Zeichen 280 (end of overtaking ban) or 282 (end of all restrictions).
tip: When you pass cyclists you must keep a lateral distance of at least 1.5 m in built-up areas and 2 m outside them (2020 amendment). If the lane is too narrow for that, stay behind. Examiners watch for this.

question: Which statement is correct?
options: You may stop for up to 3 minutes, but not park.
You may stop here only to load or unload.
You may stop here only if you stay in the vehicle.
You must not stop here even briefly, for example to let a passenger out. You may only wait when traffic forces you to, such as at a red light or in a queue.
explanation: Zeichen 283 forbids all stopping and parking on the side of the road where the sign stands. Even a short stop to let someone out or to load is not allowed. You may only stop when the traffic situation requires it. The ban normally runs to the next junction or to the end indicated on Zusatzzeichen.
tip: Even 'just a second' with hazard lights on to drop someone off is an offence here. The sign is easy to overlook near bus stops and junctions.

question: What does this sign mean?
options: Stopping is forbidden at all times, including for passengers.
Parking is allowed, but only with a parking disc.
Stopping for longer than 3 minutes is forbidden, so you must not park. Loading, unloading and boarding or alighting are still allowed.
Only residents may park, and everyone else may stop for 3 minutes.
explanation: Zeichen 286 forbids stopping for more than 3 minutes on the marked side of the road. Parking, meaning leaving the vehicle or staying longer than 3 minutes, is therefore not allowed. Boarding, alighting, loading and unloading are exempt. The ban runs to the next junction or to the end indicated on Zusatzzeichen.
tip: If you leave the vehicle, you are parking, and that is not allowed here, except while loading or unloading. Do not walk away "just for a moment".

name_de: Beginn eines eingeschränkten Haltverbotes für eine Zone
name_en: Start of a zone with restricted stopping ban
question: Which statement is correct?
options: The restricted stopping ban applies in the entire zone, on all its roads, until Zeichen 290.2 or until the zone ends. Parking is only allowed where marked parking areas or Zusatzzeichen permit it.
The ban applies only to the road where the sign stands and ends at the next junction.
This sign marks a zone where you may park anywhere for 3 minutes without a parking disc.
This sign introduces a 30 km/h zone.
explanation: Zeichen 290.1 starts a zone in which the restricted stopping ban (as for Zeichen 286) applies on all roads. Stopping for more than 3 minutes is forbidden, with the usual exceptions for loading and boarding. The zone ends with Zeichen 290.2. Marked parking areas and Zusatzzeichen can still allow parking.
tip: Unlike a single Zeichen 286, a zone does not end at the next junction. Look for Zeichen 290.2 and for the Zusatzzeichen at the entrance. Many drivers wrongly assume the ban ends after the first crossing street.

question: What does this sign mean?
options: Parking is forbidden here.
Parking is permitted here, subject to conditions shown on Zusatzzeichen (such as time limits, parking disc, fee or permit holders only).
Only parking on the pavement is permitted.
Parking is allowed at any time and without conditions.
explanation: Zeichen 314 marks a parking place or area where parking is permitted. Zusatzzeichen add conditions: maximum time with parking disc, fees, permit-holder-only, vehicle types, and the way you must park (parallel, diagonal, perpendicular). You must follow those conditions exactly. An arrow or symbol shows the layout.
tip: The Zusatzzeichen is the legally decisive part. Read the whole signpost, including days and times, before you leave the car. A fine often results from overlooking small plates.

question: Which statement is correct?
options: Parking on the pavement is allowed in the way shown on the sign. Pedestrians must be left enough room, and the permission applies only to vehicles up to 2.8 t gross weight.
Parking is allowed on the pavement for any vehicle without restriction.
You may stop on the pavement, but not park.
Parking on the pavement is forbidden, but you may use the cycle lane.
explanation: Without this sign, parking on a Gehweg is forbidden. Zeichen 315 allows it, and the symbol shows how: fully or partly on the pavement, parallel or at an angle. It applies to vehicles up to 2.8 t permissible gross weight. Pedestrians, including people with prams and wheelchairs, must still be able to pass. Zusatzzeichen can add limits.
tip: Check the sign symbol for which wheels may go on the pavement. If a pram or wheelchair could not get past, you are parking too far in, even where the sign allows it.

question: What does this sign mean?
options: Pedestrians and cyclists share this path.
The path is for cyclists only. Cyclists must use it, and other vehicles must not drive on it.
Cyclists may use the path, but are allowed to use the road too.
Mopeds may also use the path.
explanation: Zeichen 237 marks a cycle path (Radweg) reserved for cyclists, who must use it (Benutzungspflicht). Motor vehicles must not drive, stop or park on it.
tip: Before turning right, check the cycle path with a shoulder check. Cyclists going straight have priority. Lorries over 3.5 t must also turn right at walking speed in built-up areas (2020 amendment).

name_en: Shared path for pedestrians and cyclists
question: Which statement is correct?
options: Pedestrians and cyclists have separate lanes, and each group stays in its own lane.
Only pedestrians may use this path, and cyclists must use the road.
Cyclists have priority on the path and pedestrians must give way.
Pedestrians and cyclists share this path. Cyclists must use it but must not endanger or obstruct pedestrians, so they may need to slow down or wait.
explanation: Zeichen 240 marks a shared path with no dividing line. Cyclists are obliged to use it, and pedestrians may walk on all of it. Cyclists must show consideration for pedestrians, adapt their speed, and wait if necessary. Motor vehicles may not use the path.
tip: Here the path has no dividing line. A line between two pictograms means Zeichen 241, a separated path. Mixing them up is a very common exam error.

question: What must you do when you see this sign?
options: Cyclists and pedestrians share the whole path equally.
Only cyclists are allowed on the path.
Pedestrians and cyclists must each use their own part of the path, as shown by the pictograms. The path is closed to motor vehicles.
Cyclists may choose between the cycle part and the road.
explanation: Zeichen 241 shows a path split into a cycle part and a pedestrian part, with each pictogram on its own side of a dividing line. Cyclists must use the cycle side and pedestrians the footpath side. Motor vehicles may not use the path. Note that the pedestrian-only path (Sonderweg Fußgänger) is Zeichen 239, a different sign.
tip: Many foreign drivers confuse this with the shared path (Zeichen 240, no dividing line). For you as a driver: when turning across such a path, expect fast cyclists on their side.

question: What does this sign mean?
options: Cyclists and pedestrians share this path.
Pedestrian zone in which delivery vehicles are allowed.
This path is reserved for pedestrians; vehicles may not use it.
Pedestrian crossing ahead; give way to pedestrians.
explanation: Sign 239 marks a path that is reserved for pedestrians. Vehicles, including bicycles, may not use it unless a supplementary plate allows it (for example 'Radfahrer frei', which means walking speed and consideration for pedestrians). The rule applies along the path that the sign marks.
tip: As a driver you may cross a Gehweg only to reach a driveway or car park, and then you give way to everyone (§10 StVO). Never park on it unless Z 315 or markings allow it.

question: What must you do when you see this sign?
options: Not drive in, unless a supplementary plate allows it. If it does, drive at walking speed and do not endanger or obstruct pedestrians.
Drive in at up to 30 km/h; pedestrians must give way when you signal.
Drive in only if you are a cyclist; all motor vehicles are prohibited without exception.
Drive in and park at the edge, as long as you leave a lane free for pedestrians.
explanation: A pedestrian zone is closed to vehicle traffic. Only the exceptions on supplementary plates apply, for example delivery traffic at certain times or 'Radverkehr frei'. Where vehicles are allowed, they must drive at walking speed, must not endanger or obstruct pedestrians, and must wait if necessary. The zone lasts until sign 242.2 (Ende einer Fußgängerzone).
tip: Read the plate closely before you enter, because the permitted times are often limited. Even if you may enter, pedestrians keep the right of way in practice, and examiners expect you to drive at walking speed.

question: Which statement is correct?
options: All vehicles may use the street, but cyclists must ride at the right edge.
Only cyclists may use it, and there is no speed limit for them.
Cars may use it at any time, but cyclists have priority at junctions.
Other vehicles may enter only if a plate allows it. The maximum speed is 30 km/h, and cyclists may ride side by side.
explanation: A Fahrradstraße is a street for cyclists. Other vehicles may use it only if a supplementary plate allows them. The maximum speed for everyone is 30 km/h. Cyclists may ride side by side, and they may be neither endangered nor obstructed. The rules apply until sign 244.2 (Ende einer Fahrradstraße).
tip: If a plate such as 'Kfz frei' lets you in as a car driver, stay behind slower cyclists and do not overtake closely. Do not honk at cyclists riding side by side.

question: What does this sign mean?
options: A bus stop; you may not stop or park in front of it.
A lane reserved for buses on scheduled service; other vehicles may use it only if a plate allows it.
A lane for all vehicles with three or more occupants.
A parking area for buses only.
explanation: Sign 245 reserves a lane for buses on scheduled service (Linienverkehr). Other vehicles, such as taxis or cyclists, may use the lane only if a supplementary plate allows them. The rule applies to the lane that the sign marks, until the restriction ends or changes.
tip: Do not rely on the lane colour or on the lane simply looking empty. Check the sign and any plate. Using the lane without permission is a common and costly mistake for newcomers.

question: What must you do when you see this sign?
options: Honk briefly so that pedestrians know you are coming and let you pass.
Keep your speed, because pedestrians must wait for a gap in traffic.
Approach at moderate speed, let pedestrians cross who are on the crossing or clearly want to cross, and do not overtake.
Stop in every case, even if nobody wants to cross.
explanation: At a Fußgängerüberweg, vehicles must approach at moderate speed and let pedestrians (and wheelchair users) who are crossing or clearly want to cross go first. If necessary, you must wait. Overtaking is not allowed on the approach to the crossing, and you may not stop or park on it or up to 5 m before it.
tip: If a vehicle in front of you stops at the crossing, do not overtake it. A pedestrian you cannot see may be crossing in front of it. Watch the kerb for people who are about to step out.

question: What does this sign mean?
options: A danger spot ahead; adapt your speed and be ready to brake. A plate often says what the danger is.
A no-stopping zone; you may not stop or park here.
A police checkpoint ahead; have your documents ready.
A road closure ahead; you must turn around.
explanation: Sign 101 warns of a danger that is not covered by a specific warning sign. A supplementary plate usually names it, for example roadworks or an obstacle. Reduce your speed, be ready to brake, and watch the road closely. The warning applies until you have passed the danger.
tip: Always read the plate underneath, because it tells you what to expect. Slowing down early is what examiners look for.

question: What does this sign warn you about?
options: A pedestrian crossing, where pedestrians have priority.
A pedestrian zone starts here, and vehicles are prohibited.
A school or kindergarten nearby; children may run into the road.
Pedestrians crossing or walking on the road; be ready to brake and give them room.
explanation: Sign 133 is a warning sign. It warns that pedestrians may be crossing the road or walking on it, often where there is no marked crossing. It does not give pedestrians priority by itself. Reduce your speed and be ready to brake. The warning applies until you have passed the danger spot.
tip: In the city, look for people stepping out between parked cars or from behind tram stops. A blue sign with a zebra crossing is sign 350, which is a different rule.

question: Which statement is correct?
options: Children have priority here, and you must stop whenever you see one.
The sign warns of children, so you should reduce speed, be ready to brake, and watch the roadside.
The sign shows a playground; you may not drive past it.
The sign only applies during school hours.
explanation: Sign 136 warns that children may enter the road, for example near schools, playgrounds or kindergartens. It does not grant priority. You must adapt your speed to the danger, be ready to brake, and watch the roadside closely. The warning applies until you have passed the danger spot.
tip: Children are unpredictable, so cover the brake early and keep a wide gap to parked cars. Instructors watch for this in residential streets. A plate may add a time restriction; otherwise the warning is not time-limited.

question: What does this sign mean?
options: Cyclists have the right of way at the next junction.
A cycle path starts here, and cyclists must use it.
Cyclists may cross or join the road ahead; reduce speed and be ready to brake.
Cyclists are not allowed on this road.
explanation: Sign 138 warns that cyclists may cross or enter the road, for example where a cycle path crosses it. The sign does not decide who has priority. That is decided by the right-of-way rules or signs at the junction. Be ready to brake and watch for cyclists, including fast ones. The warning applies until you have passed the danger spot.
tip: Look carefully to the right and left before the crossing, because cyclists can appear quickly. Do not assume that you always have priority.

question: What does this sign warn you about?
options: A traffic-light system ahead; be prepared to stop, because it may be hard to see in time.
A railway crossing with light signals.
A junction where the traffic lights do not work.
A pedestrian crossing with a button for pedestrians.
explanation: Sign 131 warns of a traffic-light system (Lichtzeichenanlage) ahead. It is used where the lights are hard to see in time, for example after a bend or on a fast road. Reduce your speed and be ready to stop. The traffic lights themselves give the actual instruction. The sign only warns you.
tip: Do not speed up to beat an amber light. After the sign, watch the lights early and be ready to stop smoothly.

question: What does this sign mean?
options: General danger spot (Gefahrstelle) – the type of danger is shown on a plate
Roadworks ahead – workers and machinery may be on or beside the road
Slippery road surface ahead
The road is closed to all traffic after the sign
explanation: Zeichen 123 warns of a roadworks site ahead. Reduce speed early, be ready to brake and watch for workers, machinery and a narrowed or shifted lane. The sign does not close the road. Any binding speed limit or overtaking ban must be shown by separate regulatory signs, and the warning applies until the works section ends.
tip: In city roadworks the lanes are often shifted and people on foot may cross suddenly. Instructors want to see an early speed reduction and a mirror check before you reach the narrowing, not braking at the last second.

name_en: Mandatory direction of travel: turn right
question: What must you do when you see this sign?
options: You may turn right, but going straight ahead is still allowed
Right-of-way applies for vehicles coming from the right
Only buses and taxis must turn right; other vehicles may continue
You must drive in the direction of the arrow (turn right); other directions are prohibited
explanation: This blue round sign (Zeichen 209) is a mandatory-direction sign. You may only continue in the direction the arrow shows, here to the right. It applies at the junction or intersection where it is posted, so go straight or left only if another sign allows it.
tip: The sign usually stands right at the junction. Get into the right lane in good time and signal. Cutting across lanes at the last moment is a typical mistake in city lessons.

name_en: Mandatory passing: pass on the right
question: Which statement is correct?
options: You must pass the obstacle ahead (e.g. a traffic island or bollard) on its right-hand side
You must turn right at the next junction
You may pass either side, but the right side is recommended
The road narrows on the right and you must give way to oncoming traffic
explanation: Zeichen 222 stands at an obstacle in the carriageway, such as a traffic island or a roadworks barrier. You must pass it on the right, as the arrow points. It does not order a turn. The obligation applies only at that obstacle.
tip: Mixing this up with the turn-right sign 209-20 is the classic mistake. The arrow here points diagonally down past the obstacle, while the turn sign shows a plain arrow. Passing on the wrong side is a violation and very dangerous at an island.

question: What does this sign mean?
options: No entry for vehicles of all kinds
Turning left is prohibited, but U-turns are allowed
U-turns are prohibited (you must not turn around)
No overtaking on this section
explanation: Zeichen 272 shows a U-turn arrow in a red circle and prohibits turning the vehicle around to drive back the way you came. This includes turning in one move and turning in several moves, such as a three-point turn. The ban applies from the sign onward, so do not turn around until you are clear of the signed section.
tip: Turning around is also forbidden where it is unsafe or obstructive, even without this sign. Do not reverse into a driveway to turn around where the sign stands. If you miss your turn, drive on and use a roundabout or a loop of side streets.

question: Which statement is correct?
options: Entering this road is prohibited for all vehicles
The road has no through route for vehicles; you may enter, but you will have to turn around or return
Priority road ends and right-before-left applies
Parking is only allowed in this street
explanation: Zeichen 357 informs you that the road ahead is a dead end for vehicles. It does not prohibit entering and does not change priority rules. Variants of the sign with an additional symbol can show that pedestrians or cyclists may still get through.
tip: Look carefully at the lower part of the sign. A through-way for cyclists or pedestrians does not mean you can drive through. Do not reverse long distances in a narrow dead end. Find a safe place to turn and watch for playing children.

name_en: Green arrow (right turn on red allowed after stopping)
question: Which statement is correct?
options: You may turn right on red without stopping if nobody is visible
The sign allows you to drive straight on at red if the road is clear
You must stop at the stop line first, and may then turn right only if you do not endanger or hinder anyone
The sign applies to buses and trams only
explanation: The green arrow on a black plate (Zeichen 720) beside a red traffic light allows a right turn on red. First stop at the stop line. Then turn only if you cannot endanger or hinder others, especially pedestrians and cyclists crossing and the cross traffic. The permission covers only the right turn.
tip: A complete stop is the point instructors watch for. A rolling stop counts as a mistake. The arrow plate is not the same as an illuminated green-arrow light, which is a signal and has its own rules.

question: What does this sign mean?
options: The speed limit shown on the sign ends here; the general limits apply again
All speed limits and overtaking bans end here
You may now drive at any speed you like
A minimum speed ends here
explanation: Zeichen 278 cancels the speed limit with that number that was signed earlier. The general limits apply again: 50 km/h in built-up areas, 100 km/h for cars outside them (on motorways there is no general limit, 130 km/h is only recommended). It ends only the speed limit, not an overtaking ban or other bans.
tip: In town this sign never means 'free speed'. Check whether you are still in a built-up area and keep 50 km/h. A common trap is expecting it to cancel an overtaking ban as well. Only Zeichen 280 or 282 do that.

question: What must you do when you see this sign at a level crossing?
options: You have priority over rail vehicles if you are already driving on the crossing
Cross at normal speed, because trams always yield in town
Stop only if a barrier is closed; otherwise drive on
Give priority to rail vehicles; if a train or tram approaches, or a signal or barrier says so, you must wait before the crossing
explanation: The Andreaskreuz (Zeichen 201) means that rail vehicles have priority at this crossing. Approach slowly, look both ways and wait if a train or tram is coming. Red flashing lights, a barrier or an acoustic signal also mean you must wait. Never stop on the tracks.
tip: In cities this sign often marks tram crossings without any barrier. Look for trams even when the tracks seem quiet. Do not queue on the tracks. Only enter if your exit is clear and you will not have to stop on the crossing.

question: Which statement is correct?
options: Stopping and parking are completely forbidden everywhere on this street
It marks a bus or tram stop; you must not park within 15 m before and after the sign, and must not obstruct public transport
It marks a taxi rank where only taxis may wait
It marks a stop where all vehicles must stop and wait for a signal
explanation: Zeichen 224 marks a stop for buses or trams. Parking is not allowed up to 15 m before and after the sign. You may stop briefly only if no public transport is impeded. When a bus or tram is standing at the stop, take extra care for passengers who get on or off.
tip: Do not pass a standing tram or bus if passengers are crossing the road to reach it. Wait behind it. Only pass at very low speed and with enough distance if there is room and nobody is endangered.

question: What does this sign mean?
options: Only the speed limit ends; an overtaking ban remains
All traffic bans in the whole city end, including parking bans
All route-based bans, such as speed limits and overtaking bans, end here
A zone with a speed limit ends here and you may drive without limit
explanation: Zeichen 282 (white round sign with black diagonal stripes) ends all section-based prohibitions previously ordered, such as speed limits and overtaking bans. After it, the general rules apply again, for example 50 km/h in a built-up area. It does not cancel parking or stopping bans, or restrictions from other zones.
tip: Do not treat it as permission to speed up. In town you are still limited to 50 km/h unless another sign says otherwise. Do not mix it up with 278, which ends only a speed limit.

name_en: Lane boundary and carriageway edge line (solid line)
question: Which statement about a solid white line (Zeichen 295) is correct?
options: You may cross it to overtake as long as there is no oncoming traffic.
It is only a recommendation to stay in lane; crossing it is allowed with care.
It only applies to vehicles over 3.5 t.
You must not drive on or over it.
explanation: A solid line separates lanes (Fahrstreifenbegrenzung) or marks the edge of the carriageway (Fahrbahnbegrenzung). It is a prohibition: you may not cross it or drive on it. This applies to all vehicles, whether or not other traffic is present, until the line ends or becomes a broken line.
tip: Beginners often straddle a solid line while avoiding a cyclist or a parked car. Instructors watch for this, because even driving on the line counts as a violation. A broken line with long strokes (a warning line) often announces that a solid line is coming.

name_en: Broken guide line (lane divider / centre line)
question: What does a broken white line with short strokes and longer gaps (Zeichen 340) mean?
options: It is a solid-line prohibition, so overtaking is forbidden.
It guides you in your lane. You may cross it, for example to overtake or turn, if you do not endanger anyone.
It marks the end of a no-stopping zone.
It marks a lane reserved for buses.
explanation: The Leitlinie (Zeichen 340) separates lanes or marks the carriageway edge, and it helps you keep your position. Unlike the solid line (Zeichen 295), crossing it is not prohibited in itself. You may cross it to overtake, change lanes or turn, but you must not endanger or obstruct anyone. A line with strokes longer than the gaps is a warning line and announces a solid line ahead.
tip: Crossing the line does not mean you have right of way. Check mirrors and shoulder over the line, and always signal. Treat a line with long strokes and short gaps as 'solid line coming soon'.

name_en: Directional arrows on the road surface
question: What must you do when you are in a lane with arrow markings (Zeichen 297) pointing left and straight ahead?
options: Turn right at the next junction, since arrows are only a suggestion.
Use the lane only to continue straight or turn left at the next junction or intersection.
Turn in any direction, because the arrows only apply to buses.
Stop before the arrows and wait for a green signal.
explanation: Richtungspfeile prescribe which directions you may take from that lane at the next junction or intersection. With a left-and-straight arrow you may go straight or turn left, but not turn right. The marking applies at that junction, so choose your lane in good time.
tip: In city traffic, read the arrows early and change lanes before the markings begin. Last-minute lane changes across a solid line, or turning against the arrow, are classic faults. Foreign-licence drivers often assume arrows are only advisory, but in Germany they are binding.

question: What does a surface marked with diagonal stripes within a solid border (Zeichen 298) mean?
options: It is a reserved parking area.
It is a bus lane that other vehicles may use briefly.
Vehicles must not use it: no driving, no stopping, no parking.
It is a lane for turning vehicles only.
explanation: A Sperrfläche is closed to vehicles. You may not drive onto it, stop on it or park on it. It is often used to guide traffic around islands, junction approaches and lane shifts, and the ban applies at all times.
tip: Do not cut across a Sperrfläche to dodge a queue or to reach a lane faster. Instructors treat it as an obvious violation. Do not confuse it with the zigzag line (Zeichen 299), which only forbids stopping.

name_en: Boundary marking for no-stopping / no-parking zones (zigzag line)
question: What does a yellow zigzag line along the edge of the road (Zeichen 299) mean?
options: Parking is allowed there for up to 3 minutes.
It marks a lane for cyclists only.
It shows where a road narrows.
It marks a no-stopping zone along the zigzag line, so you may not stop or park there.
explanation: The zigzag line is a Grenzmarkierung. It marks the length of a stopping and parking ban, commonly at bus stops and similar places. Do not stop or park along the marked stretch.
tip: Do not stop 'just for a moment' to drop off passengers. At bus stops in particular you block public transport, and this is a typical fault on a driving test. Allow extra space when you are following buses.

question: What does this sign mean?
options: A double bend, first to the right
A road that ends in a left turn only
A dangerous left-hand curve ahead
A one-way street turning left
explanation: This warning sign shows a left-hand curve ahead that you cannot always judge well in advance. Reduce speed in good time and stay in your lane, because speed must be adapted to the curve. The warning applies until you have driven through the curve.
tip: Brake before the curve, not in it. In the city, a curve often hides pedestrians or cyclists, so keep to the right and look through the bend. Do not cut the curve, because oncoming traffic is a real risk.

question: Which statement is correct for this sign?
options: Two left curves follow directly, with no change of direction.
Two curves follow one after the other, the first to the left and the second to the right.
Overtaking is generally forbidden from now on.
The road is slippery in the next two bends.
explanation: The Doppelkurve warns of two consecutive curves in opposite directions, and here the first curve is to the left. Adjust your speed so that you can safely handle both curves. The sign does not itself prohibit overtaking, but visibility is limited and overtaking is often impractical.
tip: Do not speed up when the first curve ends, because the second one comes immediately. A common trap is to read the sign as a single curve and brake too late. Check the symbol to see which direction comes first.

question: What must you do when you see this sign?
options: Prepare for a steep downhill section, adjust your speed and use engine braking if needed.
Switch off the engine to save fuel.
Give way to vehicles coming uphill.
Overtake slow vehicles before the slope.
explanation: Zeichen 108 warns of a downhill gradient. The figure on the sign, for example 10 %, gives the gradient in percent. Adjust your speed, maintain safe following distance and use engine braking, for example by changing down a gear, so your brakes do not overheat. The warning applies until the descent ends.
tip: In the city, steep descents make braking distances longer, especially in wet or icy conditions. Instructors watch for early gear changes and a larger distance to the vehicle ahead. Do not coast in neutral.

question: What does this sign mean?
options: A steep downhill section ahead
A steep uphill section ahead
The road ahead has an uneven surface
Vehicles over a certain weight must use a crawler lane
explanation: Zeichen 110 warns of an uphill gradient ahead. The percentage on the sign shows how steep it is. Change down in time and keep up momentum, and expect slow vehicles such as lorries or cyclists. The warning applies until the climb ends.
tip: A frequent test error is stalling on a hill start with a car behind you. Practice using the handbrake smoothly and keep a larger gap to the car ahead. Check which way the sign's slope tilts, so you do not confuse it with 108.

question: Which statement is correct?
options: The road ahead has bumps or dips, so you must reduce speed.
The road ahead is slippery because of leaves or mud.
The road ahead has a steep downhill section.
The road ahead is unpaved gravel only.
explanation: Zeichen 112 warns of an uneven road surface, for example bumps, dips or speed humps. Slow down early enough to keep control and avoid damaging the vehicle. The warning applies for the stretch of road where the surface is uneven.
tip: Cyclists and motorcyclists are especially vulnerable on uneven surfaces and may swerve, so leave room. Brake before the bump, not on it. This sign often appears before speed humps in residential areas, so watch your speed and the road ahead.

question: What does this sign mean?
options: Slippery road: speed limit of 30 km/h until the next junction
Winter-tyre obligation applies from here on
Danger of skidding or sliding, for example on a wet or dirty road surface
Skid-training area ahead: only vehicles with ESP may enter
explanation: The sign warns that the road surface can be slippery because of wetness, dirt, leaves, ice or similar. It sets no fixed speed limit, but under § 3 StVO you must adapt your speed and braking distance to the conditions. It applies to the stretch where the hazard exists. A supplementary plate such as 'bei Nässe' or a length in metres can narrow this down.
tip: In the city the usual culprits are wet tram rails, cobblestones, painted markings and wet leaves. Brake early and gently, and avoid sudden steering. Instructors want to see anticipation, not just a lower speed.

question: Which statement is correct?
options: The carriageway narrows ahead, so adapt your speed and watch for oncoming traffic
You have priority over oncoming traffic at the narrow point
Overtaking is forbidden for all vehicles from here
Only vehicles wider than 2 m must give way at the narrowing
explanation: The sign warns that the carriageway becomes narrower on both sides. It does not grant or take away priority, so you must adapt your speed and be ready to brake or let oncoming vehicles pass. Priority at a narrow point is only regulated by Zeichen 208 (Vorrang des Gegenverkehrs) or 308 (Vorrang vor dem Gegenverkehr), or by the general rules of § 6 StVO.
tip: Do not assume that you have priority just because the other driver looks hesitant. Look for signs 208/308 before you enter. Also remember cyclists, who are easily squeezed at narrow points.

question: What must you expect when you see this sign?
options: The right lane is closed for HGVs only
The road narrows on both sides, so you must drive in the middle
A left-hand bend with reduced width ahead
The carriageway narrows on the right, for example because of an obstacle, so you may have to move left or wait
explanation: The sign warns that the carriageway becomes narrower on the right-hand side only. The sign itself regulates no priority. If the obstacle is on your side, § 6 StVO requires you to let oncoming traffic pass first. Unless there are other signs, the narrowing is limited to the stretch where the road is actually narrower.
tip: Check the mirror and shoulder before you move left. Cyclists riding on the right are often forced out into your path by this kind of narrowing, so leave a safe passing distance.

question: What must you do when you see this sign?
options: Leave the road at the next exit because of a closure
Be prepared for slow or stationary traffic ahead and brake in good time, and use hazard lights if necessary
Switch off the engine as soon as the first car stops
Use the left lane to pass the queue and merge later
explanation: The sign warns that there is a traffic jam or very slow-moving traffic ahead. Reduce speed early, brake gently and keep your distance. At the back of a jam you may switch on your hazard lights (Warnblinkanlage, § 16 StVO) to warn the traffic behind you. The warning applies to the stretch ahead, until the jam has dissolved.
tip: On multi-lane roads outside built-up areas and on motorways you must form an emergency lane (Rettungsgasse) once traffic slows to walking pace (§ 11 StVO). In the city, watch for sudden queues behind curves and tunnel entrances.

question: What does this sign mean?
options: One-way street ahead, no entry from the opposite direction
Road works with alternating one-way traffic
Warning: oncoming traffic on a road section that was previously one-way or had separate carriageways
Overtaking is permitted because the road is wide enough for two vehicles
explanation: The sign warns that you are entering a section with two-way traffic, usually after a one-way section or a road with separate carriageways. Keep to the right, adapt your speed and expect oncoming vehicles. The warning applies until the road ahead is clearly two-way.
tip: After a one-way system or a dual carriageway, drivers sometimes stay too far left out of habit. Move to the right deliberately. Examiners notice if you cut right bends or overtake at once.

question: What must you do when you see this sign?
options: Reduce speed and be ready to brake, because wild animals may cross, especially at dusk and dawn
Stop and wait until all animals have passed
Hooting loudly is mandatory here
Drive at least 70 km/h to leave the danger zone quickly
explanation: The sign warns that wild animals such as deer or boar may cross the road. Reduce speed, be ready to brake and watch the road edges. It applies to the stretch ahead, usually until the end of the wooded or open area. Speed must always suit conditions (§ 3 StVO).
tip: Do not swerve violently for an animal; brake in a straight line. After a collision, secure the scene with hazard lights, call the police (110) and do not take the animal with you. This also matters on roads at the city edge near parks and woods.

question: Which statement is correct?
options: You have priority over rail vehicles if you approach slowly
A level crossing with full barriers is ahead, so you only need to stop when they are closed
Railway traffic is forbidden here, so you can cross freely
A level crossing without barriers is ahead; rail vehicles have priority, so approach with great care and be ready to stop
explanation: The locomotive symbol warns of a level crossing without barriers. At the crossing itself, the Andreaskreuz (Zeichen 201) gives rail vehicles priority over road traffic (§ 19 StVO). Reduce speed, look both ways and listen. If a train is coming, wait before the crossing.
tip: Never stop or queue on the tracks, and do not enter if traffic ahead may hold you on the crossing. If your vehicle stalls on the tracks, get everyone out and away from the line immediately, then call for help.

question: What does this sign mean?
options: You may turn left or go straight, as you wish
At the next junction you may only continue to the left
Left-hand traffic is mandatory from here
You must turn left immediately after the sign, even before the junction
explanation: Vehicles may only continue in the direction of the arrow. The sign is a mandatory direction sign and applies to the junction or intersection at which it stands, so you may only turn left there. Other directions are prohibited unless a supplementary plate allows an exception. It applies until you have passed that junction.
tip: Get into the correct lane early and indicate in good time. Going straight 'because nobody is coming' is still a violation. Watch for supplementary plates that may allow exceptions, for example for cyclists.

question: Which statement is correct?
options: You must go straight ahead for the next 500 m, wherever the road leads
You may go straight or turn right
At the junction where the sign stands you may only continue straight ahead and must not turn left or right
You must stop and then continue straight ahead
explanation: The straight arrow orders vehicles to continue straight ahead only. It applies at the junction or intersection where it stands, so turning left or right there is prohibited. Zeichen 209-30 also does not allow you to turn around. It applies until you have passed that junction, unless a supplementary plate adds exceptions.
tip: Do not confuse it with signs that allow two directions, such as 214 (straight or right). Look carefully at the arrow shape. Examiners notice drivers who shift lanes late and then 'correct' the direction.

question: What must you do when you see this sign?
options: Turn left at this point, because you may only continue in the direction of the arrow
Go straight to the next junction and turn left there
Turn left only if the road is clear, otherwise go straight
Keep left until the end of the street
explanation: The sign with the angled arrow orders you to turn in the direction shown at the place where the sign stands. It is a mandatory direction sign; going straight or turning the other way is prohibited. Unlike Zeichen 209, which applies at the junction ahead, the 'hier' version applies at the sign's own position. It applies until you have made the turn.
tip: Check the exact position of the sign. If it stands at a driveway or a bend, you must turn there and not at the next junction. As always, check mirrors and shoulder, signal and give way to pedestrians and cyclists when turning.

name_en: Mandatory direction: straight ahead or right
question: What must you do when you see this sign at a junction?
options: You may only continue straight ahead or turn right; turning left or making a U-turn is prohibited.
You may turn in any direction, but you must give way to traffic coming from the right.
You must turn right at the next junction and may not continue straight ahead.
You may only continue straight ahead; turning right is prohibited.
explanation: The sign prescribes the permitted directions at the next junction or crossing: straight on or right. Left turns and U-turns are not allowed there. It applies at the junction where it is placed. Priority rules still apply as usual.
tip: Check your lane position early. Instructors watch for drivers who see the sign too late and cut across to the left. The sign shows only the allowed directions, not who has priority.

name_en: One-way street (traffic flows to the left)
question: Which statement is correct?
options: The street is closed to all vehicles in both directions.
Vehicles may only drive in the direction of the arrow (to the left); driving the opposite way is not allowed.
Left turns are mandatory at the next junction.
Traffic in both directions is allowed, but the left lane has priority.
explanation: The sign marks a one-way street where traffic may only move in the direction of the arrow, here to the left. It is placed at the junction where the one-way section begins and repeated along it. Driving the opposite way is prohibited unless a Zusatzzeichen allows it for specific road users, for example cyclists.
tip: Look for a Zusatzzeichen under the sign. Cyclists are often allowed to ride against the flow, but car drivers must expect them. Never enter from the opposite end: that end is normally marked with Zeichen 267 (Verbot der Einfahrt).

name_de: Verbot für Kraftfahrzeuge mit einer zulässigen Gesamtmasse über 3,5 t
name_en: No motor vehicles over 3.5 t permissible gross mass (lorry ban)
question: Which statement is correct?
options: All motor vehicles including cars are prohibited.
Only vehicles that are actually loaded with more than 3.5 t are prohibited.
Only vehicles carrying hazardous goods are prohibited.
Motor vehicles over 3.5 t permissible gross mass, including their trailers, and tractors are prohibited. Cars (Pkw) and buses are exempt.
explanation: The sign bans lorries and similar motor vehicles whose permissible gross mass (zulässige Gesamtmasse) is over 3.5 t, including their trailers, and also tractors. Cars and buses are exempt. The ban applies from the sign up to the next junction or as limited by a Zusatzzeichen.
tip: The ban refers to the permissible mass written in the vehicle papers, not the current load. Heavy motorhomes and vans with a high gross mass can be affected. Check the registration document, not just what is on board.

question: What does this sign mean?
options: Cyclists must use the cycle path to the right of the road.
Bicycles are prohibited from stopping here, but may pass.
Cyclists are not allowed to ride here.
Cyclists have priority over all other traffic.
explanation: The sign prohibits cycling on this road or path. Cyclists must take another route or push their bike as pedestrians would. For you as a driver it tells you that you will not normally meet cyclists on this stretch, but a Zusatzzeichen may allow exceptions.
tip: Do not mix it up with the blue Zeichen 237 (Radweg), which obliges cyclists to use a path. Here the prohibition sign is red and round. Cyclists who ignore it do occasionally appear, so stay alert.

name_de: Verbot für Krafträder, auch mit Beiwagen, Kleinkrafträder und Mofas
name_en: No motorcycles (including with sidecar), mopeds/light motorcycles and mofas
question: Which vehicles are prohibited by this sign?
options: Only motorcycles over 125 cc.
Cars and motorcycles, but not mopeds.
All two-wheeled vehicles including bicycles.
Motorcycles (also with sidecar), Kleinkrafträder (mopeds) and Mofas.
explanation: The sign bans motorcycles, including those with sidecars, as well as small motorcycles (Kleinkrafträder, e.g. mopeds) and Mofas. Cars and bicycles are not covered. The ban applies from the sign to the next junction unless a Zusatzzeichen states otherwise.
tip: Cars may pass this sign. Don't confuse it with Zeichen 260 (car and motorcycle pictured), which bans all motor vehicles.

question: What does this sign mean?
options: Pedestrians are not allowed to use this road or path.
Pedestrians must use the opposite side of the road.
Pedestrians have right of way at this point.
Pedestrians may only cross the road here.
explanation: The sign prohibits pedestrians from using the road or path. It is often found on fast roads or at tunnels. It applies from the sign to the next junction unless a Zusatzzeichen changes this.
tip: Drivers rarely see it, but it signals that the road is not designed for people on foot, so traffic may be faster. Do not confuse it with Zeichen 250, which closes the road to all vehicles but not pedestrians.

name_de: Verbot für Fahrzeuge über angegebene tatsächliche Masse
name_en: No vehicles over the stated actual weight
question: What must you check when you see this sign with a weight figure (e.g. 5.5 t)?
options: The permissible gross mass shown in the vehicle registration document.
The axle load of your heaviest axle only.
The actual weight of your vehicle including load and passengers.
Only whether you are driving a lorry.
explanation: The sign prohibits vehicles whose actual mass, including load and passengers, exceeds the stated value. The figure applies to the vehicle as it is right now, not to the registration papers. It is typically used before weak bridges or roads.
tip: This one is about actual weight, so a heavily loaded van can be affected even if its permissible mass is lower. Compare with Zeichen 253, which relates to the permissible mass and a fixed 3.5 t.

name_de: Verbot für Fahrzeuge über angegebene Breite einschließlich Ladung
name_en: No vehicles over the stated width (including load)
question: Which statement is correct for a sign showing a width of 2 m?
options: Only vehicles over 2 m wide with no load are prohibited.
Vehicles wider than 2 m, including their load, may not pass.
Vehicles must keep 2 m lateral distance from parked cars.
The road narrows to 2 m, but all vehicles may enter.
explanation: The sign prohibits vehicles whose actual width, including load, exceeds the stated figure. Mirrors may matter if they extend the vehicle's width. It protects narrow passages, and you may not enter even if you think you can squeeze through.
tip: Think of wide loads, trailers and large vans with mirrors folded out. Do not confuse it with the warning sign for a road narrowing (Zeichen 120), which only warns but does not ban.

name_de: Verbot für Fahrzeuge über angegebene tatsächliche Höhe einschließlich Ladung
name_en: No vehicles over the stated actual height (including load)
question: What does this sign mean?
options: A warning that the road ahead has a low underpass, but all vehicles may enter.
Vehicles with an actual height including load above the stated figure are prohibited.
Only trucks must check their height; cars may pass.
The height limit refers to the permissible vehicle height from the registration document.
explanation: The sign bans vehicles whose actual height, including load, exceeds the figure shown. It is used for low bridges, tunnels or underpasses. It applies to all vehicles, not only lorries.
tip: Remember roof boxes, bikes on the roof, aerials and roof racks: they count toward the height. If you are unsure, take another route. Instructors like to ask about this with loaded vans or roof cargo.

name_de: Beginn eines Verkehrsverbots zur Verminderung schädlicher Luftverunreinigungen in einer Zone
question: What must you have before entering a zone marked with this sign?
options: Nothing, the sign only recommends clean vehicles.
A vehicle allowed by the Zusatzzeichen, usually shown by the correct Umweltplakette (environmental sticker) on the windscreen.
A toll vignette for the city centre.
A special parking disc.
explanation: The sign marks the start of a zone where vehicles with high emissions are not allowed. The Zusatzzeichen below it shows which Umweltplakette colour is required for entry. The zone applies until it is ended by Zeichen 270.2. All vehicles must comply, including foreign-registered ones.
tip: Check the sticker before you enter. If you have a foreign-registered car, you must still obtain a valid Umweltplakette for the zone. Do not assume a vehicle that is considered clean elsewhere is automatically allowed.

name_de: Überholverbot für Kraftfahrzeuge mit einer zulässigen Gesamtmasse über 3,5 t (und Zugmaschinen)
name_en: No overtaking for motor vehicles over 3.5 t permissible gross mass (and tractors)
question: Which statement about this sign is correct?
options: It prohibits overtaking for all motor vehicles, including cars.
It prohibits overtaking only for motor vehicles with a permissible gross mass above 3.5 t, including their trailers, and for tractors. Cars and buses are exempt.
It prohibits overtaking only for vehicles carrying dangerous goods.
It is a recommendation for lorries to avoid overtaking in the city.
explanation: Zeichen 277 bans overtaking of multi-track motor vehicles for lorries over 3.5 t permissible gross mass (including their trailers) and for tractors. Cars and buses are not covered. The ban applies from the sign until a Zeichen 281 or until the end of the stretch as shown by a Zeichen 282 or by a junction/road change. Note: older textbooks and some image databases still say '2.8 t', which is outdated. Check the current threshold of 3.5 t.
tip: As a car driver you are not addressed by this sign. In the symbol the overtaking vehicle is a red lorry; in Z 276 it is a red car, and that one applies to you.

name_de: Ende des Überholverbotes für Kraftfahrzeuge aller Art
name_en: End of the overtaking ban for all motor vehicles
question: What does this sign mean?
options: End of the overtaking ban for motor vehicles over 3.5 t only.
End of all prohibitions and restrictions, including speed limits.
End of the overtaking ban for motor vehicles of all kinds (ends Zeichen 276).
Overtaking is now mandatory for slow vehicles.
explanation: Zeichen 280 ends the overtaking ban imposed by Zeichen 276 for all motor vehicles. From the sign on, overtaking is allowed again under the general rules of §5 StVO. Other bans such as speed limits stay in force until they are cancelled separately.
tip: 'Overtaking allowed' does not mean 'overtaking safe'. Check for oncoming traffic, junctions, solid centre lines and a clear view before you pull out. Instructors watch for people who accelerate past the sign without checking.

name_de: Ende des Überholverbots für Kraftfahrzeuge mit einer zulässigen Gesamtmasse über 3,5 t
name_en: End of the overtaking ban for motor vehicles over 3.5 t permissible gross mass
question: Who is addressed by this sign?
options: All motor vehicles, because the overtaking ban for everyone ends here.
Only motorcycles and mopeds.
Cars and buses only; lorries must continue to avoid overtaking.
Lorries over 3.5 t permissible gross mass (and tractors), for whom the ban of Zeichen 277 ends.
explanation: Zeichen 281 cancels the overtaking ban of Zeichen 277 for lorries over 3.5 t (including their trailers) and tractors. After this sign these vehicles may overtake again under the general rules. For cars, nothing changes because the ban never applied to them.
tip: Look at the symbol: the lorry on the sign tells you which ban ends. If you see only cars in the symbol (Z 280), the ban for all motor vehicles ends. Don't confuse the two.

name_de: Ende eines eingeschränkten Haltverbots für eine Zone
name_en: End of a restricted stopping zone
question: What does this sign mean?
options: The zone of restricted stopping (Z 290.1) ends here; the general rules for stopping and parking apply again.
A parking-management zone with parking discs ends here.
A zone of absolute no stopping begins here.
Parking is now allowed everywhere, even at junctions and in front of driveways.
explanation: Zeichen 290.2 ends a zone that started with Zeichen 290.1 (eingeschränktes Haltverbot für eine Zone). Inside such a zone stopping for longer than three minutes is prohibited unless a plate allows something else. After the sign, the normal rules of §12 StVO apply again, including the general bans near junctions, bends and driveways.
tip: Don't assume you may park anywhere after the zone ends. The general parking bans of §12 StVO still apply. Also keep in mind that this is not the same as the end of a parking-management zone (Z 314.2).

question: What must you do when you see this sign?
options: Nothing; the sign only shows that a car park is near.
Park only as allowed by the plates (e.g. parking disc, ticket, resident permit); the rule applies in the whole zone until Z 314.2.
Stop for at most three minutes anywhere in the zone.
Pay a toll when you enter the zone.
explanation: Zeichen 314.1 marks the beginning of a zone in which parking is regulated, for example with a parking ticket, parking disc or a resident permit. The supplementary plates under the sign show the exact conditions. The rules apply to all roads in the zone, usually without repeating the sign, until Zeichen 314.2 ends the zone.
tip: In cities you often see only the zone sign at the entrance, not at every parking space. If you can't find a plate, read the entrance sign again. Parking without a valid ticket or disc is an offence, so check before you leave the car.

question: Which statement is correct?
options: The special parking rules of the zone no longer apply after this sign.
You must leave the zone within three minutes.
Parking is now free of charge but only with a parking disc.
You may park everywhere, including where a general parking ban applies.
explanation: Zeichen 314.2 ends the parking-management zone that started with Zeichen 314.1. After this sign the zone-specific conditions (ticket, disc, resident permit) are no longer valid. The general rules for stopping and parking in §12 StVO apply, and other signs are still valid.
tip: Be careful when you park right after the sign: a single sign later in the street may start another regulated area. Always look for additional signs, not only for the end sign.

question: What does this sign mean?
options: End of a traffic-calmed area where walking speed applies.
The pedestrian zone ends here; the general traffic rules apply again.
End of a cycle street.
Pedestrians must leave the road here.
explanation: Zeichen 242.2 marks the end of a pedestrian zone that started with Zeichen 242.1. In the zone, vehicles are only allowed if a plate permits them, and then only at walking speed. After the sign normal traffic rules apply again. When you drive out of the pedestrian zone onto a road, you must make sure that you don't endanger anyone (§10 StVO).
tip: At the exit of a pedestrian zone you have no right of way. Roll out slowly, watch for cyclists and pedestrians and, if necessary, let yourself be guided. Don't confuse it with the end of a traffic-calmed area, which is Z 325.2.

question: What changes at this sign?
options: The cycle street ends; its special rules (cyclists only, 30 km/h limit etc.) no longer apply.
The pedestrian zone ends and you may drive normally.
Cyclists must now use the cycle path next to the road.
The speed limit of 30 km/h begins.
explanation: Zeichen 244.2 ends a cycle street (Fahrradstraße) that started with Zeichen 244.1. In a cycle street only cyclists may use the road unless a plate allows other vehicles, and the speed limit is 30 km/h. After the end sign the usual rules apply again, so other vehicles may use the road and the 30 km/h limit of the cycle street no longer applies.
tip: Remember that on a cycle street cyclists may ride side by side. Check your speed after the end sign: only the cycle-street limit is cancelled, and a general limit such as 50 km/h in the town may still be relevant.

question: What must you do when you see this sign?
options: Nothing special; ordinary roads and rules apply.
Follow the special motorway rules; only motor vehicles with a design speed of more than 60 km/h may use it.
Reduce speed to 50 km/h.
Give way to all traffic from the right.
explanation: Zeichen 330.1 marks the start of an Autobahn. From here the special rules of §18 StVO apply. Only motor vehicles with a design-related top speed of more than 60 km/h are allowed. Pedestrians, cyclists and slow vehicles are prohibited, and stopping and turning are not allowed. The rules apply until Zeichen 330.2.
tip: When you are new to German motorways, remember that the recommended speed is 130 km/h unless a sign limits it, and that overtaking on the right is prohibited, with only a few exceptions. Don't confuse it with Z 331.1, a road for motor vehicles (Kraftfahrstraße).

question: What does this sign tell you?
options: The motorway starts here.
The motorway ends here; the ordinary rules of the road apply, including right of way at junctions.
You must leave the motorway at the next exit.
The recommended speed of 130 km/h ends and you must drive 30 km/h.
explanation: Zeichen 330.2 marks the end of an Autobahn. The special motorway rules of §18 StVO end there and the usual rules of the road apply again. That means the normal right-of-way rules, and for example cyclists or pedestrians may be present on the road ahead depending on the type of road.
tip: After a long motorway stretch drivers often keep too much speed. Check the speed limit on the next signs and adapt your speed early, especially if a town begins directly after the end of the motorway.

question: Which statement is correct for this sign?
options: Only passenger cars may use this road; trucks and motorcycles are excluded.
Only motor vehicles with a design speed of more than 60 km/h may use this road, and stopping on the carriageway is prohibited.
You must drive at least 60 km/h on this road, otherwise you are blocking traffic.
All Autobahn rules end here and normal city traffic rules apply again.
explanation: The sign marks a Kraftfahrstraße. Only motor vehicles whose construction allows more than 60 km/h are permitted. Pedestrians, cyclists, mopeds (Mofas) and slow vehicles such as tractors are not. Stopping on the carriageway is prohibited. The rule applies until the sign Ende der Kraftfahrstraße (331.2).
tip: The 60 km/h refers to the vehicle's design speed, not to a minimum speed you must drive. A Kraftfahrstraße can be an urban Bundesstraße with junctions, so do not treat it like a full Autobahn. Instructors watch for hesitant stopping on the carriageway, which is not allowed.

question: What does this sign mean?
options: End of the Autobahn; the speed limit of 50 km/h applies from here.
End of the Kraftfahrstraße; from here other road users such as cyclists may be allowed again.
Start of a Kraftfahrstraße; only fast motor vehicles may enter.
End of all speed limits and other prohibitions on this road.
explanation: The sign ends the Kraftfahrstraße that started with sign 331.1. From here the special rules for motor-vehicle roads no longer apply, such as the restriction to vehicles above 60 km/h design speed and the stopping ban on the carriageway. The normal rules of the road then apply, and the road may be open to other road users.
tip: After the sign, expect slower vehicles, cyclists or pedestrians to appear. Adjust your speed and check for junctions or crossings. Do not assume that other signs, such as speed limits, end here too.

name_en: Arrow sign – exit from the Autobahn
question: What does this blue arrow sign on the Autobahn tell you?
options: It marks the exit from the Autobahn; if you want to leave, you take this exit.
It prohibits all traffic from using the right-hand lane.
It announces a lane reduction in 500 m.
It is a recommended direction for lorries only.
explanation: This blue arrow sign is placed at the actual exit of an Autobahn. It shows you where to leave the Autobahn. If you want to exit, follow the arrow into the exit lane. It does not forbid anything and does not limit your speed by itself.
tip: Prepare early: get into the right lane in good time, indicate, and reduce speed in the exit lane, not on the main carriageway. Slowing down abruptly on the through lane is a classic mistake that examiners criticise.

question: What is the purpose of this sign?
options: It gives the speed limit for the next exit.
It marks the end of the Autobahn.
It announces an upcoming exit or junction and shows the distance to it.
It orders you to leave the Autobahn at the next exit.
explanation: This large blue sign announces an upcoming exit or junction on the Autobahn. It usually lists the destination, the road number and the distance to the exit. It is only information; you decide whether to leave. It does not give any order.
tip: Use the announcement to plan your lane change early and signal in time. Late, hard lane changes in front of an exit are a common cause of accidents and of lost points in a driving test.

question: What does this sign mean?
options: Recommended speed of 50 km/h; you may exceed it if the road is clear.
Minimum speed of 50 km/h.
Maximum permitted speed of 50 km/h from this sign onward.
