Start of a zone with a 50 km/h limit that ends automatically at the next junction.
explanation: Sign 274 sets a binding maximum speed, here 50 km/h. It applies from the sign until it is cancelled, for example by an end-of-limit sign or by another speed sign. You may drive slower, but not faster than the limit.
tip: Inside built-up areas, 50 km/h is already the general limit. A 50 sign there can serve as a reminder after a section with a different limit. Look for signs that end or change the limit, and do not rely on 'it must be over by now'.

question: What must you do when you see this sign?
options: Drive at least 70 km/h.
Not exceed 70 km/h from here on, until the limit is cancelled or changed.
Drive exactly 70 km/h.
Reduce speed to 70 km/h only if there is oncoming traffic.
explanation: This sign sets a maximum speed of 70 km/h. It applies from the sign until it is cancelled by an end sign or replaced by another speed sign. Drive slower whenever road, traffic, visibility or weather require it.
tip: It is a maximum, not a target. Wet roads, fog or heavy traffic can require a lower speed even when the sign allows 70. Do not confuse it with the blue round minimum-speed sign 275.

question: Which statement is correct?
options: The sign is only a recommendation; the Autobahn recommended speed is 130 km/h anyway.
You must drive at least 100 km/h here.
The limit applies only to lorries.
You may not drive faster than 100 km/h from this sign until it is cancelled or replaced.
explanation: Sign 274 with 100 is a binding maximum speed of 100 km/h. It overrides any general recommended speed such as the Autobahn Richtgeschwindigkeit of 130 km/h. It applies from the sign until it is ended or replaced.
tip: On the Autobahn many drivers confuse the recommended speed with a legal limit. A red-ringed round sign is always a binding limit. A blue rectangular sign 380 is only a recommendation.

question: What must you do when approaching this marking?
options: Let pedestrians and wheelchair users who are crossing or about to cross go first; approach at moderate speed and stop if necessary.
Speed up so that pedestrians have no time to cross.
Pedestrians always have to wait for a gap in the traffic here.
Overtake slow vehicles in front of the crossing to keep traffic flowing.
explanation: The white stripes mark a Fußgängerüberweg (zebra crossing). Pedestrians and wheelchair users who are on or clearly want to use it have priority. Approach at moderate speed and be ready to stop, and stop in front of the crossing if needed. Overtaking vehicles at the crossing is prohibited.
tip: Do not overtake on the approach, and do not wave pedestrians through if the lane next to you is also blocked by a stopped vehicle. Instructors watch for early speed reduction and eye contact. Never park or stop on the crossing itself.

question: What does this broken transverse line mean?
options: You must stop completely here in every case, like at a stop sign.
It is a parking-space marking.
You must wait here if necessary to give way to traffic with priority.
Overtaking is allowed beyond this line.
explanation: The Wartelinie (341) is a broken line across the lane. It marks where you must wait if the traffic situation requires it, because someone else has priority. It reinforces a give-way obligation, for example together with sign 205 Vorfahrt gewähren. You only have to stop if there is traffic you must let pass.
tip: A broken line means 'wait if necessary', a solid line means 'stop'. At a give-way line, stop behind the line if you must wait, and roll forward carefully if your view is blocked. Do not mistake it for a Haltlinie.

question: Where must you stop when you have to stop at this marking?
options: With your front wheels on the line.
Anywhere in the junction as long as you can see cross traffic.
Just before the line, so that no part of the vehicle crosses it.
Behind the line, but only if other vehicles are waiting.
explanation: The Haltlinie is a solid transverse line. It shows where you must stop when required, for example at a red light, at a stop sign (Zeichen 206 Halt. Vorfahrt gewähren), at a level crossing barrier or when signalled by police. You must stop in front of the line, not over it. At a stop sign you may continue only when it is safe.
tip: At a STOP sign, stop with the car stationary in front of the line. If you still cannot see, creep forward slowly and stop again where you can. Rolling stops and stopping on top of the line are typical test mistakes.

question: What does this supplementary plate mean?
options: The main sign applies only to the area or road section in the direction of the arrow (to the left)
You must turn left at the next junction
The main sign applies only to vehicles that are turning left
The main sign ends at this point
explanation: An arrow plate shows the direction in which the regulation of the main sign applies. A left-pointing arrow means the regulation applies in that direction, for example along the kerb or road section to the left of the sign. It is not an order to turn. It applies for as long as the regulation of the main sign applies.
tip: Do not read the arrow as a turning instruction. In the city, check the arrow direction before you park, because the same pole may carry two signs with opposite arrows.

question: Which statement is correct for this plate below a sign?
options: The regulation applies only for the next 100 m
The hazard or regulation of the main sign begins only after the stated distance of 100 m
The speed limit is 100 km/h
You must stop after 100 m
explanation: This plate tells you that the danger or rule of the sign above starts after the stated distance, here 100 m ahead. Prepare to adapt your driving as you approach that point.
tip: Do not confuse 'nach 100 m' (distance to the start) with 'auf 100 m' (length of the stretch affected). Start looking and slowing early, so you are ready when the stated point arrives.

question: What does this supplementary plate below a sign mean?
options: Cyclists are exempt from the main sign
Cyclists must dismount and push their bikes
Cyclists are prohibited here
The main sign refers to cycle traffic, so it is directed at cyclists
explanation: A plate with a bicycle symbol shows that the main sign concerns cycle traffic. It is not a general exemption. Check which main sign it is combined with and what that sign orders or warns about. It applies where the main sign applies.
tip: Do not mix it up with 'Radfahrer frei'. This plate defines who is addressed, while 'frei' means an exemption. Cyclists and parked cars are often where city lessons go wrong, so check mirrors and shoulder before turning.

question: What does this plate mean?
options: The regulation shown by the main sign ends here
The regulation begins in 100 m
The regulation continues only on weekends
It is the last warning before a dead end
explanation: The plate 'Ende' shows that the regulation of the associated main sign ends at this point. From here you are no longer bound by the restriction. Other signs that apply on the road remain valid.
tip: A sign with 'Ende' only cancels that specific regulation, not everything else. Check what else is still in force, for example a general speed limit of the built-up area.

question: What must you do when you see this plate below a prohibition sign?
options: Drive through only if you are a resident registered in this street
Use the road freely, because the prohibition applies only at night
Use the road only if you have a destination along it (for example residents, visitors, deliveries); through traffic is not allowed
Use the road only with a residents' parking permit
explanation: 'Anlieger frei' exempts people who have a legitimate destination along the road from the prohibition. This covers residents but also visitors, customers and suppliers. Through traffic, which only uses the street as a shortcut, remains prohibited. It applies for the stretch covered by the main sign.
tip: Shortcutting through a residential street is not allowed even if it is 'only a short way'. Without a destination in the street, turn away.

question: Which statement is correct for a sign with this plate?
options: The main sign applies only to cyclists
Cyclists are exempt from the restriction of the main sign
Cyclists must give way to all other traffic
Mopeds are also allowed
explanation: 'Radfahrer frei' exempts cyclists from the prohibition or restriction of the main sign. For example, cyclists may be allowed through a road otherwise closed to vehicles. The exemption covers cyclists only, not other vehicles. It applies as long as the main sign applies.
tip: Expect cyclists where you would not normally expect traffic, such as in a one-way street from the opposite direction. Keep a safe lateral distance and watch junction exits.

question: What does this plate mean?
options: Only buses must obey the main sign
Buses may stop here at any time
Only buses are exempt from the main sign; all other vehicles must obey it
All vehicles with more than eight seats are exempt
explanation: The plate exempts buses (Kraftomnibusse) from the restriction or prohibition of the main sign. All other vehicles, including cars and trucks, remain bound by it. The exemption is valid where the main sign applies.
tip: Do not follow a bus into a restricted street just because it entered. Look for the plate that includes your vehicle type.

question: What does this plate mean?
options: The main sign applies only in the stated time window, 16:00 to 18:00, on all days of the week
The main sign applies only from Monday to Friday
The main sign applies except between 16:00 and 18:00
The main sign applies for a maximum of 18 hours
explanation: The regulation of the main sign is in force only during the stated hours, 16:00 to 18:00. Because no days are given, it applies on every day of the week, not only on working days. Outside this window the regulation does not apply.
tip: Check the clock when you park. A space that is allowed at 15:45 can become a violation at 16:00 if you stay. Also note the missing weekday information: it covers weekends too.

question: Which statement is correct?
options: The main sign applies on every day from 16:00 to 18:00
The main sign applies on weekdays from Monday to Friday, all day except 16:00 to 18:00
The main sign applies only on Mondays and Fridays
The main sign applies only from Monday to Friday between 16:00 and 18:00
explanation: The main sign is valid only on the stated days (Monday to Friday) and in the stated hours (16:00 to 18:00). Outside this time, including weekends, it does not apply. A public holiday falling on a weekday is not mentioned on the plate, so check carefully if it matters.
tip: Check both day and hour. Parking at 17:00 on Saturday is a different case from 17:00 on Thursday. Hold on to your parking disc or keep a clear note of when the regulation starts.

name_de: nur Schwerbehinderte mit außergewöhnlicher Gehbehinderung und Blinde
name_en: Only severely disabled people with extraordinary walking disability (aG) and the blind
question: What must you do when you see this plate below a parking sign?
options: Park here only if you display the matching special parking permit for severely disabled people with aG or the blind
Park here for up to 30 minutes with a parking disc
Park here only if you are over 65
Park here freely, because the plate applies only to buses
explanation: The parking space is reserved for severely disabled people with extraordinary walking disability (aG) and for blind people. They must display the corresponding special permit clearly visible behind the windscreen. Other drivers may not park there, even briefly.
tip: A normal parking permit, or no permit at all, is not enough. Do not use these spaces 'just for a minute'. Instructors count it as a clear mistake.

question: This plate is mounted under a speed-limit sign. Which statement is correct?
options: The speed limit applies only when the road surface is wet.
The speed limit applies only while it is actually raining, not on a wet surface after the rain stops.
The speed limit applies only in the first 100 m after the sign.
The speed limit is a recommendation in wet conditions and not binding.
explanation: The Zusatzzeichen 'bei Nässe' limits the sign above it to times when the road surface is wet. The limit applies from the sign until it is cancelled or the road ends or changes. When the road is dry, the sign above it does not apply.
tip: A road can still be wet after the rain has stopped, and the limit still applies then. Assume that a damp surface counts as 'Nässe', and adjust your speed to what the road is like now.

name_en: Stopping ban also applies on the hard shoulder / verge
question: What does this plate mean when it is shown with a stopping-ban sign?
options: Stopping is allowed on the shoulder but not on the carriageway.
The stopping ban applies only on the carriageway, and the shoulder may be used for parking.
The stopping ban also applies on the Seitenstreifen (shoulder), not just on the carriageway.
The shoulder is reserved for emergency vehicles only.
explanation: The plate extends the stopping restriction of the sign it is attached to, so it also covers the hard shoulder or verge next to the road. You may not stop or park there either, within the area the main sign covers.
tip: Don't assume a wide verge is a safe place for a 'quick stop'. If the plate is there, the shoulder is covered by the ban just like the carriageway.

question: Which statement about this sign is correct?
options: It warns of a stretch where strong side winds may push the vehicle off course.
It shows that the road is closed to light vehicles in windy weather.
It indicates a nearby airport and low-flying aircraft.
It permits you to drive faster, since a tailwind helps you.
explanation: The sign warns of strong gusts from the side, for example on bridges, embankments or open stretches. Slow down, hold the steering wheel firmly with both hands, and watch for lateral drift, especially when passing trucks or leaving a sheltered stretch. The warning applies to the section ahead, as far as the danger lasts.
tip: Be careful when overtaking cyclists or trucks in gusty conditions, because the wind can push you sideways. Give extra lateral space.

question: What does this warning sign tell you?
options: There is a level crossing ahead with barriers or gates.
There is a level crossing ahead without any barriers.
Trains have priority only when the barriers are lowered.
A tram crossing ahead has priority over you, but trains do not.
explanation: The sign warns of a level crossing with barriers (Schranken) ahead. At the crossing, rail traffic has priority, and the Andreaskreuz (Zeichen 201) marks that priority. You must wait in front of the crossing when a barrier is closing or closed, when red lights flash, or when a train is approaching.
tip: Never stop on the tracks. Before you cross in slow-moving city traffic, make sure there is space for your car on the other side. Zeichen 151 shows a level crossing without barriers and is not the same.

name_en: Three-bar distance marker (left side) before a level crossing with barriers
question: What does this sign tell you?
options: A level crossing is exactly 300 m away.
It is the last warning, and the crossing is directly ahead.
It is the first of three markers, and the level crossing with barriers is still some distance ahead.
The crossing ahead has no barriers, and you must stop.
explanation: Baken count down the distance to a level crossing. The three-bar marker is the first and the farthest from the crossing, followed by the two-bar and one-bar markers. Outside towns the three-bar marker is typically at roughly 240 m, but spacing can vary. You can use the markers to judge how far away the crossing is and to slow down in time.
tip: A marker on the left side is a version for the left. Follow the same pattern: three bars, then two, then one. In a city a crossing can be close, so watch for it with signal lights and barriers.

name_en: Hard shoulder may be used as a lane
question: Which statement is correct when you see this sign?
options: The hard shoulder is reserved for breakdowns and is still closed to normal traffic.
The hard shoulder may be used as an additional lane from here.
You must leave the hard shoulder immediately.
The hard shoulder may be used for parking.
explanation: Zeichen 223.1 opens the Seitenstreifen as a driving lane on the road, usually on an Autobahn when traffic is heavy. From the sign you may drive on the shoulder as a lane, and the rules for lane use then apply. The opening applies until the sign 223.2 or another sign changes it.
tip: This sign is not for city lessons, but it can come up in the test. A shoulder open as a lane is not an emergency lane, and breakdowns need special care. Look at the signs on gantries for the current status.

name_en: Hard shoulder no longer to be used as a lane
question: What does this sign mean?
options: The hard shoulder is now open as an extra lane.
The hard shoulder may now be used for stopping and parking.
The hard shoulder is closed for repairs for the next 5 km.
From here the hard shoulder may no longer be used as a driving lane.
explanation: Zeichen 223.2 ends the shoulder opening that was started by Zeichen 223.1. From here the Seitenstreifen is a shoulder again and not a lane. If you are driving on it, move back into the regular lanes in good time and with consideration for other traffic.
tip: The pair of signs (223.1 and 223.2) is a start and an end. Remember that the end is not a place to stop, since the shoulder is only for emergencies again.

question: What must you do when you see this sign?
options: Park there if you have a hotel booking.
Treat the area as a bus stop, where you may stop briefly.
You may stop for up to 3 minutes to let passengers out.
Do not stop or park there with a car that is not a taxi, because the space is reserved for taxis.
explanation: Zeichen 229 marks a taxi rank, where only taxis may wait for passengers. Other vehicles may not park or stop in the marked area. The area runs along the sign's marked length or the road markings, which show where the rank starts and ends.
tip: Stopping 'just for a moment' to drop someone off is a common mistake. Instructors and traffic wardens look for it. The sign for bus stops is Zeichen 224 (Haltestelle), which is different.

question: Which statement is correct for this sign?
options: Horse riders may use this path, but cyclists may also use it if they ride slowly.
The path is a shared path for pedestrians and riders; both have equal rights.
The path is reserved for riders. Other road users, including cyclists and motor vehicles, must not use it.
The sign only advises riders to avoid the carriageway; the carriageway remains open to everyone.
explanation: The sign (Zeichen 238, Sonderweg Reiter) marks a path reserved for horse riders. Other road users, including cyclists and drivers, may not use it. It applies along the path it marks. Where the path crosses a road, normal right-of-way rules for that junction apply.
tip: Cyclists and cars often drive onto a bridleway by mistake in suburbs and park edges. Watch for the horse symbol, and if you meet riders near the path, give them plenty of room and slow down so you do not startle the animals.

name_de: Verbot für kennzeichnungspflichtige Kraftfahrzeuge mit gefährlichen Gütern
name_en: No vehicles carrying dangerous goods that require hazard marking
question: What does this sign mean?
options: Motor vehicles that must display hazard-goods markings (Gefahrgut) because of their load may not pass.
Only vehicles carrying goods that are hazardous to water are banned.
Vehicles over a stated weight are banned from this road.
All trucks are banned from this road, whether or not they carry dangerous goods.
explanation: Zeichen 261 bans motor vehicles that, under the dangerous-goods rules, must carry warning markings (orange plates or placards) because of their load. An ordinary car without such a load is not affected. It applies from the sign onward. Supplementary plates can add exceptions or a distance.
tip: Instructors like to ask whether it affects an ordinary Pkw. It does not, because the ban depends on the load, not on the vehicle size. Do not confuse it with the water-hazard sign 269.

name_de: Verbot für Fahrzeuge über angegebene tatsächliche Achslast
name_en: No vehicles exceeding the stated actual axle load
question: What must you do when you see this sign?
options: Do not enter if the total weight of your vehicle exceeds the figure shown.
Reduce speed, because heavy vehicles may only drive slowly on this road.
Do not enter if any single axle of your vehicle, including its load, carries more than the stated weight.
Enter only if your vehicle's permitted weight, as shown in the registration document, is below the figure shown.
explanation: Zeichen 263 bans vehicles whose actual axle load, i.e. the load carried by one axle including cargo, is above the tonnage shown. The decisive figure is the real axle load, not the permitted maximum in the papers. It protects weak bridges and road surfaces. Check any supplementary plates for exceptions or distances.
tip: Do not mix up weight signs. Zeichen 262 refers to total actual weight, while 263 refers to the load on one axle. If you drive a loaded van, think about how the load is distributed.

name_de: Verbot für Fahrzeuge und Züge über angegebene Länge einschließlich Ladung
name_en: No vehicles or combinations longer than the stated length, including load
question: Which statement is correct?
options: Only vehicles carrying loads that stick out past the rear are affected.
Vehicles and combinations (e.g. with a trailer) whose total length, including load, exceeds the figure shown may not enter.
The sign gives the minimum length a vehicle must have to use this road.
The sign limits the width of the vehicle, not its length.
explanation: Zeichen 266 bans vehicles and combinations whose length including the load is greater than the figure shown. A car with a long trailer or a large load can therefore be affected even if the car itself is short. It applies from the sign onward, subject to any supplementary plates.
tip: Remember to count a trailer or a roof-loaded ladder in the total length. Width has its own sign (264), height another (265). These signs are mostly aimed at narrow old-town streets.

question: What must you do when you see this sign?
options: Change to winter tyres within the next kilometre.
Drive slowly because snow chains are recommended but not mandatory.
Fit snow chains to the drive wheels before continuing, if you want to drive on this stretch.
Keep snow chains in the vehicle, but only fit them if the road is actually covered with snow.
explanation: Zeichen 268 is a mandatory sign: motor vehicles may drive on this section only with snow chains fitted to the drive wheels. Winter tyres alone are not enough here. The rule applies on the signposted stretch. Check for any end sign or supplementary plate that limits it.
tip: You will rarely see this in a city, but it matters on trips to the Alps or the Black Forest. Learn how to fit chains before you need them, not at the roadside. Drive slowly, as chains are only suitable for low speeds.

name_de: Verbot für Fahrzeuge mit wassergefährdender Ladung
name_en: No vehicles carrying goods that endanger water
question: What does this sign mean?
options: Vehicles carrying goods that could pollute water, such as fuel or chemicals, may not enter.
All vehicles with a trailer are banned.
The road is closed to all traffic when there is flooding.
Washing your car on this road is prohibited.
explanation: Zeichen 269 bans vehicles whose cargo could pollute water, such as fuel or other substances classified as water-endangering. It is typically placed near water protection zones. It applies from the sign onward, subject to supplementary plates.
tip: A normal private car with a full tank is not what the sign targets. It concerns the cargo. Do not mix it up with the dangerous-goods sign 261. 269 is about water protection, 261 is about Gefahrgut marking.

question: What must you do when you see this sign?
options: Overtake only if you leave the stated distance in metres in front of the vehicle you pass.
Keep the distance in metres shown to the vehicle ahead only at junctions.
Keep at least 50 m to the vehicle in front, whatever number is on the sign.
If the sign applies to your vehicle, never keep less than the distance in metres shown to the vehicle ahead.
explanation: Zeichen 273 prohibits driving closer to the vehicle in front than the distance in metres shown on the sign. It applies to the vehicles the sign and its plates cover, and it continues along the signposted section. The normal rule of keeping safe distance also still applies.
tip: The number on the sign is the minimum, not a guarantee of safety. In wet weather or in a city queue you may need more. Never assume you are exempt just because you drive a car. Look at the plates.

question: Which statement is correct?
options: It is a recommended speed. You may ignore it if you wish.
You must not drive slower than the stated speed, unless traffic, road, visibility or weather conditions require it, and vehicles that cannot reach it may not use the road.
You may not drive faster than the stated speed.
It means you must drive exactly at that speed.
explanation: Zeichen 275 is a mandatory sign. You must not go slower than the stated speed, unless traffic, road, visibility or weather conditions force you to. Vehicles that cannot or may not drive that fast must not use the road. It applies until the next junction or until Zeichen 279.
tip: The sign is blue and round, which makes it a Gebot, not a limit. Learners often confuse it with the red-ringed speed limit 274. A blue number means 'at least', a red ring means 'at most'.

question: What does this sign mean?
options: All speed restrictions end here.
The speed limit shown now applies.
The minimum speed requirement ends. You may drive slower again.
The recommended speed ends here, and the road reverts to the usual limit.
explanation: Zeichen 279 cancels the minimum speed set by Zeichen 275. From this point you are no longer obliged to drive at least that speed. General rules still apply, so you must drive at a speed suited to the conditions and may not impede traffic without reason.
tip: A common trap is thinking this sign lifts a speed limit. It does not. It ends a minimum, not a maximum. A red-ringed limit is ended by 278.

question: What does this sign indicate?
options: A car park with a connection to public transport, so you can park and continue your trip by bus or train.
A car park that is free for everyone, including long-term parking for caravans.
A car park reserved for taxis.
A rest area on a motorway with a hotel.
explanation: Zeichen 316 points to a parking facility with a connection to public transport (park and ride). The sign is informational and does not itself set parking rules or fees. These come from plates and signs at the site.
tip: In city lessons, expect a question about when to use these car parks. Read the plates for fees, time limits and any restriction to public-transport users. Do not assume parking is free or unlimited.

question: What does this sign mean?
options: Park-and-ride car park where you change to public transport
Parking reserved for severely disabled drivers
Car park from which marked hiking trails start
Rest area with picnic tables and toilets
explanation: Zeichen 317 marks a car park intended for hikers, usually at the start of walking trails. It is an informational sign, so it adds no new obligation. The normal parking rules and any Zusatzzeichen (for example a fee or a time limit) still apply.
tip: Do not mix it up with the Park-and-ride sign (Zeichen 316). Always read the plates beneath a parking sign before you leave the car.

question: What must you do when you see this sign?
options: Switch on your dipped headlights (Abblendlicht)
Sound your horn before entering
Stop and check the clearance height
Reduce speed to 30 km/h
explanation: Zeichen 327 shows that a tunnel begins. Under § 17 StVO you must drive with dipped headlights in tunnels, even in daylight. The sign does not set a speed limit. Any limit comes from separate signs.
tip: Daytime running lights are not enough, because they often leave the rear lights off. Switch to Abblendlicht manually if your car's automatic system does not do it. Keep a generous distance, because you may only stop in the tunnel in an emergency.

question: Which statement is correct?
options: You may use the bay for a short rest when you are tired.
The bay is for emergencies and breakdowns only.
The bay is a loading zone for delivery vehicles.
The bay is a normal bus stop.
explanation: Zeichen 328 marks a bay where you may stop if your vehicle breaks down or you have an emergency. It is not for ordinary stopping, resting or phone calls. Leave the bay as soon as the problem is solved or help has arrived.
tip: If you have to use the bay, switch on the hazard lights straight away. On roads like these, instructors expect you to put safety first and not just leave the car anywhere.

question: What does this sign mean?
options: The motorway begins here
A service area follows in the next few hundred metres
You are entering an expressway (Kraftfahrstraße)
This is the exit where you leave the motorway
explanation: Zeichen 332 marks the exit (Ausfahrt) from the motorway. Use the exit lane to leave. The sign gives no speed limit, but you should not slow down on the main carriageway. Brake only once you are in the deceleration lane.
tip: Decide early which exit you need. Motorway exits are only allowed at junctions (Anschlussstellen). A last-second swerve across the lanes is an obvious fault in a driving test.

question: What does this sign show?
options: The number of the motorway you are driving on (here A 999)
The number of a Bundesstraße
The number of a European road
The number of the next exit
explanation: Zeichen 405 is a blue road-number sign with the letter A and a number. It identifies the motorway (Autobahn). It is purely informational and carries no rule. Use it with the direction signs to follow your route.
tip: Remember the sign colours for navigating: blue for Autobahn (A), yellow for Bundesstraße (B), green for European roads (E). Confusing them is a common beginner mistake in lessons.

question: Which statement is correct?
options: It shows that the motorway starts ahead.
It gives destinations and direction on a Bundesstraße.
It marks a diversion because of roadworks.
It gives you priority at the next junction.
explanation: Zeichen 415 is a direction sign used on Bundesstraßen. It shows destinations and the direction to them. It is purely informational, so it does not grant right of way or change any speed limit.
tip: Use the arrows to choose your lane early. A late lane change at a junction is a typical examiner's complaint in town traffic.

question: What does this sign mean?
options: Motorway rules apply from this sign onwards
A motorway service area lies ahead
The motorway is closed
It points the way to the nearest motorway access
explanation: Zeichen 430 is a direction sign that leads you to a motorway entrance. You are not yet on the motorway, so the usual city rules still apply. Motorway rules only begin at Zeichen 330.1 (Autobahn).
tip: Keep to the speed limit until you are really on the slip road and the acceleration lane. Check the mirrors, signal, and merge without forcing others to brake.

name_en: Direction sign to local destinations (e.g. station)
question: What does this sign mean?
options: A railway station is the only destination on this road
Trains cross the road ahead
It points the way to a destination in town, here the railway station (Bahnhof)
Parking is reserved for station users
explanation: Zeichen 432 is a white direction sign for destinations inside a town, such as the station, city centre or a hospital. It is purely informational and does not change priority or any speed limit.
tip: Do not stop for a last-minute check of the signs, especially near airports. Use your satnav earlier and follow the arrows in good time.

question: What does this sign mean?
options: It shows a table of the speed limits ahead
It lists several destinations with arrows and distances
It lists the parking zones in the town
It gives a map of the diversion
explanation: Zeichen 434 is a table-style direction sign. It lists several destinations, usually with arrows and often distances. It is only a guide. It sets no rules about speed, priority or lane use.
tip: Read the table before the junction, not at it. Searching for your destination while stopped in the traffic flow is a typical city-driving error.

question: What does this sign mean?
options: It names the street you are on or that crosses here. It is purely informational and gives no right of way.
It marks a priority road (Vorfahrtstraße) with the street name shown.
It is a signpost to the next town, shown with its name.
It marks a residential zone (verkehrsberuhigter Bereich) with a street name.
explanation: Zeichen 437 (Straßennamenschild) only shows the name of a street, often at junctions or on a building wall. It orders nothing and does not regulate right of way. It applies only as orientation information.
tip: Do not read anything about priority into the sign. At a junction, look for Zeichen 306, 205 or 206, or apply 'rechts vor links'. Do not let street-name hunting distract you from pedestrians and cyclists.

name_en: Advance direction sign for specific types of traffic
question: Which statement is correct?
options: It is a speed limit that applies to the vehicle types shown.
It is a general stop sign for the lane ahead.
It announces a detour that all road users must follow.
It announces, ahead of a junction, the route recommended for the specific traffic type shown, for example heavy goods vehicles.
explanation: Zeichen 438 (Vorwegweiser für bestimmte Verkehrsarten) stands before a junction and shows which route is signposted for a specific type of traffic. It is a recommendation with no own prohibition. A matching Wegweiser (Zeichen 442) often follows at the junction.
tip: If the symbol shown does not apply to you, the sign is not aimed at you. Use the normal Wegweiser instead. In city traffic, watch which lane the sign leads you into.

name_en: Advance direction sign to the Autobahn
question: What does this sign tell you?
options: The Autobahn starts immediately here, and Autobahn rules apply at once.
It shows ahead how to reach the Autobahn at the junction and which direction it leads.
A detour around the Autobahn is signposted.
A rest area is coming up in 1 km.
explanation: Zeichen 440 (Vorwegweiser zur Autobahn) is a blue advance sign in front of a junction. It points the way to the Autobahn and often shows the junction layout. It is purely informational. Autobahn rules apply only from Zeichen 330.1 onwards.
tip: Choose your lane early in the city. A last-minute lane change right in front of the junction is a typical mistake in lessons. Remember that the Autobahn rules start with Zeichen 330.1, not with this advance sign.

name_de: Wegweiser für bestimmte Verkehrsarten (Kfz über 3,5 t, linksweisend)
name_en: Direction sign for specific traffic types (motor vehicles over 3.5 t, pointing left)
question: What must you do when you see this sign?
options: All vehicles must turn left here.
Only motor vehicles with a permissible gross mass over 3.5 t have to follow the signposted route, here to the left.
Motor vehicles over 3.5 t are prohibited in this street.
Everyone must follow the route, because it is a detour.
explanation: Zeichen 442 (Wegweiser für bestimmte Verkehrsarten) gives the direction for the group shown, here motor vehicles over 3.5 t. The arrow points left. For other drivers it has no meaning, and they follow the normal Wegweiser.
tip: In an ordinary car you are not addressed. Be careful, though: a truck turning from a left-pointing lane may swing wide, so keep your distance when it turns.

name_en: Advance exit beacon on the Autobahn
question: What does this sign mean?
options: A road works section begins in 300 m.
The Autobahn ends in 100 m.
A speed limit will start soon.
It marks the distance to an exit ahead, in steps of 300 m, 200 m and 100 m, shown by the number of stripes.
explanation: Zeichen 450 (Ankündigungsbake) stands at the right edge before an Autobahn exit. Three red stripes mean 300 m to the exit, two mean 200 m, one means 100 m. The sign is purely informational.
tip: Move to the exit lane in good time and avoid braking sharply on the main carriageway. Examiners watch your checks in mirror and shoulder (Schulterblick) before you leave the right-hand lane.

question: Which statement is correct?
options: It shows the minimum following distance between vehicles.
It lists the speed limit for the next kilometres.
It shows the distance to the next exits or destinations along the Autobahn.
It marks a rest area where you may stop.
explanation: Zeichen 453 (Entfernungstafel) is placed on the Autobahn after a junction or exit. It shows the distances to upcoming destinations along the route. It does not regulate traffic.
tip: Use these boards to plan which lane you need well before the exit. This is a common weakness among drivers new to German motorways.

question: What must you do when you see this sign?
options: Follow the arrow while the detour is signposted; it leads around a blocked section.
Turn right at once, because no other direction is allowed.
Leave the road at the next exit.
Park at the right edge of the road.
explanation: Zeichen 454 (Umleitungswegweiser) shows the way of a detour, for example around a blocked section. Follow the signs one after another until the detour ends. It is a guidance sign, not a turn command like Zeichen 209.
tip: Do not lose the next detour sign at the next junction. If you miss one, stop safely or turn around at a suitable place instead of guessing. In city traffic watch for cyclists and pedestrians on the detour as well.

question: What does this sign mean?
options: The detour has just ended.
A detour begins ahead, and this sign announces it before the junction.
Entering a one-way street is forbidden for all vehicles.
A road works zone begins with speed limit 30 km/h.
explanation: Zeichen 457.1 (Umleitungsankündigung) announces ahead that a detour starts. It gives early information so you can choose your lane in time. Afterwards you follow the Umleitungswegweiser (Zeichen 454 and similar).
tip: Use the advance notice to look at the signs calmly and choose your lane early. Do not turn into the blocked road because you think you know a shortcut. The sign itself does not order anything.

name_en: Plan sketch (diagram of the detour or junction layout)
question: Which statement is correct?
options: It shows a map of the one-way streets of the whole city.
It is a prohibition sign for the street shown.
It gives an overview drawing of the route or junction situation, for example how the detour runs.
It marks a permanent bypass for heavy goods vehicles.
explanation: Zeichen 458 (Planskizze) gives a simplified drawing of the traffic layout, for example a detour or the junction layout ahead. It is only information and orders nothing. The actual rules come from the other signs.
tip: Read the sketch before the junction, not while you are already moving through it. Look at it once and then watch the road again.

question: What does this sign mean?
options: A permanent detour for all road users on this road.
It shows a route to follow when the Autobahn is blocked and the diversion is ordered. Otherwise you ignore it.
The road ahead is closed for all vehicles.
The Autobahn ends and a normal road begins.
explanation: Zeichen 460 (Bedarfsumleitung), usually with a U and a number, marks a prepared diversion route. It is used only when needed, for example if the Autobahn is blocked by an accident and traffic is led off it. If there is no blockage, you do not follow it.
tip: Do not follow the U signs without a reason, such as a blocked road or a traffic message. Watch for signs and for police instructions, which override the plan.

question: Which statement is correct about this sign?
options: It prohibits all traffic from entering the road ahead.
It permanently replaces the normal route, so every driver must follow it.
It guides traffic along a signed diversion route (marked with a U-number) that is used when the normal route is closed or blocked.
It shows that the road ahead is a dead end.
explanation: This is an informational sign (Richtzeichen), not a prohibition. It marks a prepared alternative route, identified by its U-number, which drivers use only when the main route is closed or congested, for example after a motorway closure. If you are diverted, follow the signs with the same U-number until the diversion ends or you rejoin your original route.
tip: In unfamiliar areas, keep following the same U-number at every junction. If one sign is missing, do not guess: stop safely, check the navigation, and rejoin the U-route. Examiners like to see that you read signs ahead instead of relying only on the sat-nav.

question: What must you do when you see this sign at a parking space?
options: Place a correctly set parking disc visibly behind the windscreen and observe the permitted parking time.
Pay at a ticket machine and put the receipt on the dashboard.
Park only if you hold a residents' parking permit.
Park for free for an unlimited time, as the sign only shows that the parking space is public.
explanation: The sign tells you that parking is allowed only with a parking disc. Set the disc to the next half-hour mark after your arrival time and place it clearly visible behind the windscreen. The maximum parking time is shown on the sign or on a supplementary plate, and it applies in the times shown there.
tip: A very common trap is setting the disc to the exact minute of arrival instead of rounding up to the next half hour mark. Also remember that the disc must be readable from outside, and you cannot reset it while you are still parked there. If you do not have a disc, buy one at a petrol station or an ADAC office before you start city driving.

question: What does this sign mean?
options: A series of two curves, the first to the right
Turning right is mandatory at the next junction
Right of way changes to the right at the next junction
A single curve to the right ahead; reduce speed and be ready to brake
explanation: This warning sign (Gefahrzeichen) announces a single curve to the right. It does not set a speed limit, but you must adapt your speed to the curve and conditions and keep to the right. In built-up areas warning signs stand shortly before the hazard, outside them usually 150–250 m before.
tip: Instructors watch whether you brake before entering the curve and do not cut into the oncoming lane, especially when cyclists or parked cars narrow the road. The direction of the curve is shown by the sign graphic itself, so read the symbol and not just the number.
